I will keep things simple and steady this year. I am 71, so I will not spread myself across too many crops or try anything risky. In Quzhou, what I know best and what fits my land and labor is the wheat-maize rotation. That gives me one winter crop and one summer crop on the same land, and it matches our local weather, machines, and irrigation habits. I would rather grow the crops I understand well, use improved seed, and manage fertilizer and water carefully than chase a higher return with crops that need more labor or more technical skill.

So I will plant winter wheat first and then summer maize after the wheat harvest. I will use improved seed instead of traditional seed because I want stable emergence, stronger disease resistance, and more reliable yield, but I will avoid management that is too complicated. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and faster for me than deep ploughing and works with the equipment I can get locally. I will put enough nitrogen for grain production, with phosphorus and potassium to keep the soil from running down. I will irrigate a few key times rather than too often, because water costs money and too much water is wasteful. For pests and disease, I will spray only as much as needed to keep the crop safe, not more. My goal is not the absolute highest yield. My goal is a crop plan I can actually manage well from planting to harvest.
